title: Output of the inventaire-assets agent: the assets to add to the registry before writing the plan sheets, and the reference images of every plan

assets.description: The assets the registry does not contain yet and that the plans call for. Empty if the registry is enough. Each asset appears only ONCE, even if it is used in twenty plans.

code.description: Proposed code, prefixed by the type (PROP_lanterne, DEC_phare_nuit). The final code is rebuilt according to the registry's convention.

parent.description: ALWAYS answer. MANDATORY for a state of a recurring subject (the same set at night or destroyed, the same prop broken, the same character at another age or durably transformed; never a character on fire, glowing, wounded or as a silhouette, which stays prose in the plans): the code of the BASE subject (from the registry, or proposed here), same type as this asset. It is the starting image of the state; the registry is flat, so a state of a state also points to the base subject. `null` only for an independent asset (a distinct prop, a new character, an effect from `brief.elements`). For a `keyframe`, leave empty and list the elements to combine in `raison`.

element.description: ALWAYS answer. When the asset comes from an entry of `brief.elements`: that entry's `nom`, copied exactly. A `vfx` is accepted ONLY with this field (an effect the brief does not list stays prose in the plans). `null` for any other asset.

description.description: (French) What it is, as in the registry: what is seen, with no framing or plan light. A character: appearance only (no place, pose, action or dialogue). A set: the place only (no list of props). An asset from `brief.elements`: built from its description, colour, size and behaviour.

plans.description: The titles of the plans (as given in the input) where the asset appears.

raison.description: (French) Why no registry asset fits: what must really differ in the image.

references.description: ONE entry per plan of the input, in the input's order: the assets whose images the video model receives for that plan. Checked by the code: every code exists (registry, `assetsDejaProposes`, or `assets` above), no sound, 6 images at most.

plan.description: The plan's `id` from the input (P01, P02...), copied exactly.

codes.description: Asset codes in this order: the characters who speak in the plan, the other characters seen, props, effects, then the ONE set last. One sheet per character (never two states of the same character), one set, a keyframe only if the plan's intention names it, never a voice or a sound. Usually 2 to 5 codes; empty only for a plan with nothing to show (black screen).

notes.description: (French) Doubtful matches, registry assets you preferred over a new one, plans that seemed to call for an asset without you creating one. Empty if nothing to say.
